item.title: Dynasty confirmed. Stegall delivers in clutch as Carroll claims 4A volleyball three-peat
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS — Fort Wayne Carroll claimed its third straight IHSAA Class 4A volleyball state championship Saturday night, taking out an upset-minded Center Grove, 3-1 (25-16, 25-18, 22-25, 25-17), at Gainbridge Fieldhouse. "You think you kind of get used to it, but I'm still so excited. What a way to finish out," senior outside hitter Sarah Stegall beamed. "We believed we could do it and coming out here and actually putting our beliefs to work — it's incredible." Stegall finished with a match-high 18 kills on .268 hitting. She single-handedly orchestrated a championship-clinching 6-1 run in the fourth set , a sensational conclusion for the likely Miss Volleyball finalist, who finished her high school career with 988 kills. That gaudy career total came despite missing almost her entire sophomore season due to injury. The Notre Dame commit returned last season and flourished behind 2025 Indiana Miss Volleyball Bailey Sinish, before taking the reins of this year's attack and accumulating 481 terminations with a hitting percentage around .360. "Sarah's been our go-to all year and she stepped up in big moments," Sinish said. "I was so proud of her because she started out really strong, then we kind lost her a little bit in the middle, but she came back through when we needed her most and that's what a senior should be doing. … In the big moment, we were gonna give her the ball and she was ready to take care of it." Stegall played closer, but reaching that point of the match was a group effort, one that began with fellow attacker Katelyn Peters. The Chargers junior — and heir apparent to the No. 1 attacker spot — registered a double-double with 17 kills and 13 digs. She accounted for three kills in the decisive fourth set: The first knotted the frame at 11, the third sustained the final run, pushing the score to 18-14. Junior middle blocker Paityn Lauck, who missed most of the regular season due to injury but returned in time for regionals, capped her comeback with her best performance of the season, notching 11 kills on .409 hitting with a block, an ace and a dig. Stegall, Peters and Lauck's contributions came with senior setter Elli Oskey running the offense to the tune of 45 assists. Her individual effort, which also included seven kills (.333 hit%), pushed her season total to 1,025 — up from 330 the year before. And then, of course, there was libero Cala Haffner. The 2028 Texas commit racked up 23 digs and served four aces in her final match of the season, leading a defensive effort that saw Carroll rack up 64 kills and limit CG to .119 hitting. "This is just a special group of girls who love the game, love to have fun out there and who love each other," Sinish said. "They are ready for that big moment. It got a little tight in the middle and they started to play a little hesitant, but they made the switch and that was huge." item.title: Giants Lose Derrick Henry As Plan B In Trade Talks
item.description: James Lang-Imagn Images The New York Giants have lost their backup plan for a running back upgrade. The Baltimore Ravens made it clear they will not trade veteran star Derrick Henry to his former coach, John Harbaugh. This news closes the door on a potential deal for the 32-year-old rusher, leaving the Giants to look elsewhere before the deadline on Tuesday. Adam Schefter reported that the Ravens have “informed Henry that they have no intention of trading him” to Harbaugh and the Giants, or anywhere else. Baltimore sits at 4-5 after a tough loss to the Jaguars, yet they refuse to give up on this season or their long-term plans with quarterback Lamar Jackson. The Giants were hoping Henry could step in as a fallback option if their main target, Jonathan Taylor, proved too expensive to acquire. The Ravens Stand Firm on Henry Baltimore needs Henry to stay on the field to help them win now. The team holds a massive lead in the rushing stats, with Henry sitting seventh in the NFL at 689 yards this season. Trading him would send a bad message to Jackson, who carries a huge $84 million cap hit for 2027. The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones noted that cutting ties with a top runner would hurt the relationship with the star quarterback. “If you’re Jackson and you see your team cut ties with one of the greatest runners of a generation, what would you think?” Jones wrote. “Is that an organization invested in winning with you in 2026, 2027 and beyond?” They have 5 draft picks coming up and a schedule full of winnable games against teams like the Chargers and Panthers. Dale Zanine-Imagn Images A Shift to Justice Hill With Henry off the table, the Giants focused on a different Ravens player. Schefter reported that “A league source told ESPN that the one Ravens running back that the Giants inquired about was Justice Hill.” Hill is 28 and has spent his whole career with Baltimore. Hill has 240 rushing yards this year and 20 catches for 111 yards. He scored Baltimore’s only touchdown in the loss to Jacksonville on a 65-yard run. The Giants need depth because Tyrone Tracy Jr. is on injured reserve with a hamstring strain, and Cam Skattebo is listed as doubtful for the upcoming game. Hill could serve as an emergency fill-in, though his resume does not suggest he is a better option than Tracy. The Taylor Deal Looms Large The Giants still hold out hope for a bigger move involving Jonathan Taylor of the Indianapolis Colts. Since the Colts have already turned down a bid involving a second- and fifth-round pick, the asking price stays high. New York may need to include Tracy in a trade offer to keep some draft capital while securing Taylor. The team faces two critical divisional games against the Eagles and Commanders around the trade deadline. The next test for the Giants comes on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 1 p.m. ET against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field.

item.title: Three takeaways from Michigan State's massive win over Michigan
item.description: Michigan State football earned a massive win on Saturday evening, earning a win over their archrival, Michigan, 15-6. After a lackluster season, the Spartans bowed up in the biggest game of the year, and they earned a win over their rival to propel Pat Fitzgerald's first season in East Lansing. In the win, Michigan State outgained Michigan 298-to-192, and won the turnover battle 4-to-0. The differnences in both proved to be the difference in Michigan State earning a program win over Michigan. Take a look at our three takeaways from the win from the Spartans on Saturday night: 1. Alessio Milivojevic was a gamer After dealing with a hand injury, Michigan State starting quarterback Alessio Milivojevic gutted it out to play in this rivalry game, and he excelled. Despite a strong Michigan defense, Milivojevic stayed poised and continued to make the right read play after play to lead the MSU offense. After a season of uncertainty, Milivojevic finished 21-of-32 for 188 yards and led the MSU offense to enough points to earn a massive rivalry win. 2. Pat Fitzgerald needed this This year has been disaster for Fitzgerald, who was 2-6 and 0-5 in the Big Ten heading into this game. If there was ever a time to get his first Big Ten win, Fitzgerald needed this win against Michigan. Not only did Fitzgerald generate a ton of momentum for his program, he gave his team a chance to compete for the rest of the season with a massive momentum boosting win. 3. Joe Rossi Michigan State defensive coordinator had a lot of questions surrounding his job security, and in the biggest game of the season, he had his unit ready in a massive way. With countless injuries, and major impact players missing, Rossi had a gameplan that was exactly what the Spartans needed. MSU's defense turned out their best performance of the year, forcing four turnovers and only allowing 198 yards of offense. If anything comes out of this game, Rossi has showed his worth to Michigan State. item.title: ‘We had a chance’: Lane Kiffin baffled after LSU loss to Alabama
item.description: Sep 19, 2026; Oxford, Mississippi, USA; Louisiana State Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin looks on during the second quarter against the Mississippi Rebels at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images The No. 14 LSU Tigers moved the ball up and down the field against No. 5 Alabama on Saturday night, outgaining the Crimson Tide by 172 yards in Baton Rouge. But that didn’t matter much on the scoreboard, as LSU fell 31-13 for its third loss of the season. After the game, head coach Lane Kiffin admitted that he was struggling to make sense of it. Kiffin pointed to some impressive individual numbers from his offense and said he couldn’t believe they only added up to 13 points, calling the loss “really disappointing.” LSU’s Rough Night LSU entered the season with national title expectations in Kiffin’s first year in Baton Rouge, after he rebuilt the roster through the transfer portal. But the Tigers had already lost twice entering Saturday’s game against Alabama, including an emotional loss to Ole Miss , Kiffin’s former team, and an overtime loss at Kentucky. On Saturday, LSU went 0-for-4 on fourth down, the most attempts without a conversion in Kiffin’s career. The Tigers also made four trips to the red zone and came away with just one touchdown and one field goal. LSU briefly took the lead late in the third quarter, but Alabama answered with a 32-yard punt return by Ryan Coleman-Williams. On the next play, Keelon Russell hit Cederian Morgan for a 25-yard touchdown, and the Crimson Tide scored the final 21 points of the game. The loss dropped LSU to 6-3, and its chances of making the College Football Playoff fell from 51% to 25%, according to ESPN’s Allstate Playoff Predictor. ‘We had a chance’ After the game, Kiffin pointed out that his offense put up plenty of yards, but it didn’t translate to points. “I was looking at a sheet and it said Sam [Leavitt] had 380 yards passing and Jackson Harris had 11 [receptions] for 166 [yards] and Trey’Dez [Green] had 10 [receptions] for 85 [yards]. I wouldn’t think that would equal 13 points,” Kiffin said, via ESPN’s Alex Scarborough . “But you got to score touchdowns in the red zone.” When asked what’s keeping his team from making winning plays, Kiffin didn’t have much of an answer. “I don’t know,” he said. “We had a chance.” Kiffin also admitted that he didn’t expect LSU to be 6-3 at this point in the season, and things won’t get any easier next week, as LSU hosts Arch Manning and a Texas team coming off a controversial win over Missouri . “No, I did not think that, but it is where we are, and we can’t change that. So, we got to go back to work. Don’t have time to sit around and feel bad. Got a top-10 team coming in here in Texas,” Kiffin said. “It’s one thing, probably the one good thing about playing these types of teams in a row like this, ‘Hey, you got a chance to play another national game and get back on track,'” he added. item.title: ‘You’re an Uso’- Roman Reigns hints at Sami Zayn’s Bloodline return after Crown Jewel
item.description: Photo by Alex Bierens de Haan/Getty Images Roman Reigns has seemingly opened the door for Sami Zayn to return to The Bloodline after delivering an emotional message to his former stablemate following their match at Crown Jewel. Reigns defeated Zayn to become the 2026 Men’s Crown Jewel Champion, adding another title to his collection as WWE World Heavyweight Champion. However, the biggest talking point came after the match, when Zayn approached Reigns and asked him to shake his hand after pushing him to his limits. Roman Reigns’ message to Sami Zayn sparks Bloodline reunion talk Rather than accepting the handshake, Reigns pulled Zayn into a hug and delivered a seven-word message that immediately caught the attention of WWE fans. “You’re not an honorary,” Reigns said. “You’re an Uso.” The moment was a callback to Zayn’s previous time with The Bloodline, when he went from being an outsider to one of the faction’s most important members. Reigns’ words could now signal a change in their relationship, particularly with The Bloodline facing a growing threat from The 9-4-6. The faction currently has the numbers advantage, and bringing Zayn back into the fold would give Reigns another established star to rely on. Zayn is also a former Undisputed WWE Champion and has already shown that he can go toe-to-toe with Reigns. His performance at Crown Jewel may have given The Tribal Chief another reason to trust him. For Zayn, the message could mean more than simply being welcomed back into the group. During his previous run, he was never fully accepted by Reigns, despite becoming a key part of the faction. A reunion would also give WWE the chance to revisit one of its most popular recent storylines, with Zayn now potentially returning as a respected member rather than an outsider. For now, Reigns’ words could simply have been a callback to their shared history. But with The 9-4-6 looming, Zayn’s next move could have a major impact on the future of The Bloodline. item.title: Louisville Defeats Georgia Tech, 44-17
item.description: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - NOVEMBER 7: Tre Richardson #0 of the Louisville Cardinals runs with the ball before scoring a touchdown against the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets during the second quarter at Bobby Dodd Stadium on November 7, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Colin Hubbard/Getty Images) | Getty Images What a lovely evening. Despite the odd start with special teams blunders, I think most would agree this was the most complete performance of the season thus far. This team has had similar blow out wins against FSU and Stanford, but in those games it took a minute for the team to hit the gas a turn away. But in this one it never felt like Georgia Tech was in the game. After scoring on the first drive, the defense had to force multiple 3-and-outs to start their game before they finally conceded 3 points thanks to the special teams. Brohm looked as equally as frustrated as the rest of us, but it didn’t last long as the offense looked unstoppable and the defense looked….good? The game in its entirety was as close to perfect as fans have been hoping for all season, and for it to come in November when there’s still 3 very important games ahead could not be better timing. Lincoln looked in control all game as he finished 17/25 for 182 yds and 2 TDs, to go along with his 81 yards on the ground. Treyshun Hurry did a fantastic job filling in for the injured McCoy as he reeled in 8 receptions for 104 yards and a TD. The Brown Bros. rushed for a modest combined total of 92 yards on just 16 carries against one of, if not the worst rushing defenses in the conference. But it didn’t matter as the offense got pretty much whatever they wanted. And I’d be remiss if I didn’t mention this gorgeous jet sweep to Tre Richardson for a 52-yard TD, his second of the night. TRE RICHARDSON. AGAIN. 🤯 📺 @accnetwork x @LouisvilleFB pic.twitter.com/Ntf6DFlkql — ACC Football (@ACCFootball) November 8, 2026 Meanwhile on the defense they made life hell for whoever was playing QB tonight. Tech couldn’t seem to figure out what would work between Mendoza and Adamson, and it wasn’t much of anything between the two. The defense held Ga. Tech to an outstanding 4 of 17 on 3rd down, and 5.4 yards per pass and just 3.4 yards per rush. But the biggest numbers of the night came from the defensive front as they had 4 sacks, 7 TFLs, and 5 batted balls. It seemed like even when the commitee of QBs got time to throw, there was either pressure coming and/or hands blocking throwing lanes. It was a fantastic effort from the defense and one that I think we all hope the team can build on as they entire the final quarter of the season with a lot left on the table. It’s not often you get to kick your feet up and watch your team trounce a conference foe while other certain teams are getting blown out. So enjoy nights like tonight. We’ve all earned this one.

item.description: IND 2-0 up vs NZ in ODI series: List of teams who have lost a ODI series after taking 2-0 lead originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: India lead New Zealand 2-0 after two close wins, and history now offers a warning. Only a handful of teams have thrown away such a lead in a series of five or more matches. India themselves have suffered this fate once before, and the details may surprise fans. Can New Zealand come back from 0-2 down? Full record of bilateral ODI comebacks in history India head into the third ODI against New Zealand with a 2-0 lead, though cricket history shows that such an advantage is not always the safe position it appears to be. A small group of teams have let a similar lead slip in a bilateral series, and the names on that list include India themselves. The hosts were beaten in Auckland by five wickets, a result reached under the DLS method, and then lost again in Wellington by four runs, once more through DLS. Those two results have put India in front in the five-match series, and the remaining games will decide whether New Zealand can mount a recovery. The record books say it has been done only rarely, as a 0-2 deficit has been overturned just five times in ODI series of five or more matches. The sections below set out who has managed it, how India fell short in the past, and when the rest of the current series will be played. MORE: Rahul hailed as India clinch a narrow win in Wellington Teams who lost an ODI series after leading 2-0: Full list South Africa have achieved this twice, while Bangladesh, Pakistan and Australia have each done it once. That makes it a very uncommon feat, since it has happened only five times in more than 50 years of men’s ODI cricket. The table below lists the sides that surrendered a 2-0 lead, along with the team that came back. South Africa answered by winning in Faisalabad by 13 runs and then twice in Rawalpindi, by six wickets and by seven wickets, to take the series 3-2. item.title: 4 Head Coach Candidates Ohio State Should Target If Ryan Day Leaves
item.description: COLUMBUS, OHIO - NOVEMBER 7: Head Coach Ryan Day of the Ohio State Buckeyes talks with the referees during a timeout in the second quarter of the game against the Oregon Ducks at Ohio Stadium on November 7, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. (Photo by Ben Jackson/Getty Images) Getty It’s not even Thanksgiving, and Ohio State’s football season is over after it fell to Oregon at home 41-28 on Saturday, leaving the Buckeyes with a 6-3 record. Of course, fans are blaming head coach Ryan Day, and some have even called for him to be fired. However, that seems a bit ridiculous. Day is one of the best coaches in college football, and Ohio State shouldn’t consider firing him, but if he leaves this offseason, he could take a position in the NFL. If Day leaves Ohio State this winter, here are a few candidates the Buckeyes could consider to replace him. Notre Dame HC Marcus Freeman The first call should be to Notre Dame head coach Marcus Freeman, as he has ties to Ohio State. Freeman played linebacker for the Buckeyes from 2004 to 2008 under head coach Jim Tressel. He has coached Notre Dame for five seasons and has a 50-13 record. He led the Fighting Irish to the 2024 national championship game, where he fell to Ohio State. This past offseason, there was speculation that the New York Giants wanted to bring in Freeman as their next head coach, but he declined. It would be hard to get Freeman to leave Notre Dame, but returning to where he played college football and the state he grew up in could bring him back to Columbus. Ohio State’s DC Matt Patricia Ohio State’s defensive coordinator Matt Patricia taking over the head coaching job wouldn’t be that crazy if Day jumped ship for the NFL. If Ohio State can’t land a top college football head coach, then maybe Patricia is the route the Buckeyes take. Patricia coached the Detroit Lions from 2018 to 2020 and served as an NFL defensive coordinator with the New England Patriots from 2012 to 2017. UConn HC Jason Candle Candle is an Ohio native and attended Mount Union. He has coaching experience in Ohio, from his time as a WR coach and offensive coordinator at Mount Union to his head coaching role at Toledo from 2015 to 2025. The 46-year-old head coach took over UConn this season and had a 4-4 record heading into Week 10. Many Ohio State fans have been calling for an Ohio native to take over the head coaching job for a while, and Candle could be an option. Urban Meyer This is just a thought to consider if Meyer wants to return to coaching. While it’s unlikely Meyer will coach again, this matters more if Ohio State struggles to find a head coach after Day leaves. The Buckeyes could potentially call Meyer to take over for a few seasons. Meyer coached Ohio State from 2012 to 2018, finishing 83-9 and winning the 2014 championship. It’s pretty obvious that Ohio State has the right head coach in Day and shouldn’t look to fire him because the options don’t move the needle much. item.title: Next Tour up-and-comer inches toward breakthrough victory
item.description: Get used to seeing Ben James on future PGA Tour broadcasts. Getty Images When it comes to the story of Ben James, the next PGA Tour prospect on the verge of breaking through, it’s probably best to just stick to the numbers. He’s 23 years old and best pals with Jackson Koivun, the last young buck to bust through the entryway to Tour stardom. James has zero wins in 12 tries, but four top-4s. Those finishes have come on the back of a microwave-like ability to get hot in an instant. When he opened this week’s event in Mexico with a 65 and a 64, that marked 14 rounds of 65 or better in his young Tour career. In other words, at least one mega-low round each tournament. His explanation for it is so basic that you’ll understand why we’re sticking to the numbers. “It’s difficult,” he said of the many deep rounds, “but like I said, keep missing in the correct spots and keeping the ball below the hole and give yourself opportunities where you can be aggressive putting.” On that putting note: James is just a nick above average with the flatstick, but that’s kind of the point. The best PGA Tour players are elite with the long game and ball-striking first, then they just hit it good enough to occasionally get hot with the putter. That’s what James’ game is like. He rates in the 93rd percentile with the driver (on Tour), and in the 88th percentile with his irons. Importantly, there’s no weakness. Any golf sickos who have been following the PGA Tour this fall would not be surprised to see his name atop the leaderboard of the World Wide Technology Championship — he’s been moving in this direction for some time now. But there’s a particularly tempting array of opportunities at stake here. If James gets it done Sunday, he will not automatically earn a Masters invite via the win, like many fall winners have done in the past. But he will earn enough world ranking points to jump into the top 50 in the world ranking for the first time in his career … precisely two months before the first top-50 cutoff for qualification into next year’s first major. A victory would also book his ticket onto the 2028 PGA Tour Championship Series , a platform he seems destined for, but a worthy checkpoint before 2027 even begins. All of this brings us to the most important number: that four-shot lead. James will wake up Sunday with, according to DataGolf , a 73.7% win expectancy. There are Tour winners trailing him, but the numbers are the numbers: James’ game is as good as any of them, and he’s got the cushion.
